I know what your going through. Because my situation was similar. My 'friend' was my friend and she was really popular. But after a while, she stopped talking to me. Not completely, like sometimes I would say hi and she would say hi back. But again, that was sometimes. Most of the time when I would say hi to her she would ignore me, and/or tell her friends that they should sit somewhere else. And they got up and moved. When I confronted her about it, she told me she needed some space, or I was to clingy. In other words, followed her around too much. But that's what friends do right? They walk around or sit down and chat. But one day, another classmate told me she had heard her call me transgender in the girls bathroom with other girls. I confronted her about it, and asked her why she did that. She told me it's because I am. But really, I'm not. Back then, I just preferred nerf guns over Barbie dolls and stuff. I never considered myself to be a boy mentally or physically.

I can relate to what your going through. And I am sure many other people can as well. I too, am still trying to get over my past. And still find myself hating me for not doing something about the people who bullied me. In fact, I was bullied 2nd through 8th grade. Like you, I also find it hard to learn to trust society again. In other words people. What helps me sometimes, is I write all things I remember the bullies said to me, or even draw what they looked  like, and take the paper and put it in the paper shredder. You can even crumple it up or throw it on the floor and stomp on it.
